doc.title: Ray Conniff interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 14, 1998

title: Closing remarks and goodbyes
summary: Thanks, a sound check worry, singing off mic, and talk of a future visit to Hamilton.

story.theme_name: Thanks and goodbyes: closing the interview
story.community_name: Closing thanks and goodbyes at the end of the interview

blocks.x: Well that sounds like a great way to wrap up. And I want to say on camera that I’m very grateful to you for making the trip down from L.A. also, with the things going on in your life and you’re busy, and I really appreciate your coming down. And I wish you all the best.
Gee I never listened to a sound check. I know on the kit they sent out the sound wasn’t very great, but I hope everything came out all right, but I’ve had a little rasp in my throat.
Well I also noticed on one of, on the tape that they sent that you like to sing along but it’s “off mic” you said.
Oh, yeah, yeah, I have no chops. I don’t have a good sound. Yeah I do sing along with the horns and voices, but I prefer it if they don’t get me too predominant on a mic.
Okay, well it was a great pleasure talking to you.

Thank you very much, Monk, and gee lots of success. I understand you’ve got about a hundred others, interviews like this in there. I hope some day I may get back to see you and may be able to see a little of them.
Please when you come out to view the fall colors in the east, maybe we can have you as a guest.
Okay, well I must take your card and your address along. Are you anywhere near 80 or 70? Route 70 or 80? The big east-west highways? Are you near 40? You’d be up north.
We are on the New York State Thruway, I-90.
90. Yeah. You’d be up, I’d have to go through the northern route to go through your area probably. Okay.
